1,570 likes, 79 comments - ramit on October 21, 2026: "Most people think wasting money means buying coffee. But the biggest money drains don’t feel like waste at all. They look completely normal.

Buying a car based on the monthly payment. Paying for subscriptions you forgot you signed up for. Calling luxuries “investments.” Chasing complicated financial products that promise to beat simple investing.

None of these feel like mistakes in the moment, which is exactly why they can quietly cost you far more than any latte.

Real financial progress comes from getting the big decisions right, not from feeling guilty about the small ones. And the first step is seeing where your money is actually going.

Comment AUDIT and I’ll send you my Spending Audit Guide so you can find the drains hiding in your own spending.".

22 likes, 2 comments - ramit on October 22, 2026: "A 1% fee sounds tiny. So most people never do the math.

Here’s the math: take your balance and multiply it by 0.01. With $500,000 invested, that’s $5,000 a year. With $1,000,000, it’s $10,000. And it comes out again next year, and the year after that.

So why do so many people stay? Maybe your advisor works with your parents. Maybe they’re a friend. Maybe they send a box of cookies every Christmas. So you put it off, and the fee keeps coming out.

That’s exactly how Dan felt. When he finally ran the numbers on his advisor, it was $17,000 a year. So he sent one short email. No phone call, no sales pitch. The only reply he got was, “Is there anything I can do to change your mind?”

This Saturday, I’m sharing the exact email he sent, word for word, so you can copy it.

Comment NEWSLETTER and I’ll send you the link to get Saturday’s email.".

771 likes, 46 comments - ramit on October 20, 2026: "When was the last time you and your partner actually looked at your numbers together? For most couples, it only happens four times in their entire relationship, and even then it’s pretty vague.

The couples who feel calm about money do it differently. They sit down once a month and check four numbers:

→ Fixed Costs: ideally 50–60% of take-home pay
→ Savings: 5–10%
→ Investments: at least 10%
→ Guilt-Free Spending: 20–35%

That’s it. No tracking 200 categories and no arguing over $50 at Target. So when one of those big moments shows up, you’ve already been preparing for it.

If you want an easy way to run that monthly conversation, comment MEETING to get my free One-Hour Monthly Money Meeting Guide.".

926 likes, 43 comments - ramit on October 19, 2026: "Our parents were handed a simple formula: get a good job, stay loyal, work hard, and you’ll be taken care of.

That formula isn’t working anymore. Costs keep rising, jobs feel less secure, and doing everything “right” can still leave you feeling squeezed.

And yet most of us were taught to just accept it. “You’re lucky to have a job.” “That’s just how it is.”

It doesn’t have to be. You need a different set of rules, and one of the most powerful is having more than one way to earn money.

The hardest part for most people is figuring out what they could actually sell. 

Comment CHALLENGE and I’ll send you my free challenge to find your idea. You’ll also save your seat for my live session tonight, Monday, Oct 19 at 8pm ET.".

511 likes, 19 comments - ramit on October 17, 2026: "Number 1 is where most people get stuck. 

“I’d start a business, but I don’t have any skills people would pay for.”

Everyone does. Look at what you already pay other people to do: clean your apartment, change your oil, make your dinner. None of that requires a fancy credential. It just requires being good at something someone else doesn’t want to do themselves.

If you’re not sure what yours is, ask your partner or a friend what you’re really good at. They’ll answer faster than you think.

You also don’t have to quit your job to find out if it works. Many of my students started their businesses on the side while working full time.

I started small too. My first product was a $4.95 eBook I sold from my dorm room. It made me some extra spending money. Today it’s a business that makes money while I’m on vacation, out to lunch, or asleep.

Slow and steady wins. Once you believe there are opportunities everywhere, you start seeing them.

Comment CHALLENGE and I’ll send you my free 3-day challenge to find your business idea. You’ll also save your seat for my live session on Monday, Oct 19.".
